recipes.name: Grilled Tilapia with Mango Salsa
ingredients_raw: 1 large ripe mango, peeled, pitted and diced

steps.text: Prepare the fish: Whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, parsley, garlic, basil, black pepper, and salt in a bowl and pour into a resealable plastic bag. Add tilapia fillets, coat with the marinade, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator for 1 hour.

Meanwhile, make the salsa: Combine mango, bell pepper, jalapeño pepper, red onion, and cilantro in a bowl. Add lime and lemon juices and toss well. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.

Remove tilapia from the marinade and shake off excess. Discard remaining marinade. Grill fillets until fish is no longer translucent in the center and flakes easily with a fork, 3 to 4 minutes per side, depending on the thickness of the fillets.
Serve tilapia topped with mango salsa.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Tilapia with Mango Salsa
raw_recipe.description: This spicy mango salsa for fish can be made a day ahead and paired with herb-marinated and grilled tilapia fillets for a wonderful, go-to summer meal.

video.description: A simple fresh mango salsa takes grilled tilapia to the top!

review.reviewBody:
This was delicous! I started marinading the fish just a couple hours ahead of time. Then I put the two fillets in a 9x9 pan, drizzled most of the marinade over the top, and then baked it in the oven (covered) at 350 for 15 minutes, and then I uncovered it and baked it at 375 until it was done (probably another 10 minutes, I didn't set the timer).
The salsa is great, too. It really makes enough for about 4+ fillets, but I enjoyed the leftovers with chips, so I don't know that I would ever cut the salsa recipe in half. I paired this with some coconut rice and asparagus. I'll definately make this again.

This recipe is one in a million! I don’t care for fish but my husband and I ate grilled Red snapper with mango salsa over coconut lime rice at The Coral Reef restaurant in EPCOT and I LOVED IT! He did too! As soon as we got home I searched for a mango salsa recipe like the salsa at the restaurant and this one is so close! We use it with citrus marinated salmon fillets and put it over coconut rice or coconut lime rice and add avocado slices as well. It’s so refreshing and delicious! And I found a hack to easily peel the mango! Slice the mango off center on the flatter side so there are two parts. Next slice one of those parts in half and using a rocks glass with an edge, place the mango with the flesh side facing inside the glass and gently slide the mango down the glass. It is so easy ! Then just dice the mango. Do that for the other side after you slice the middle part out. I usually slice the mango on either side of the pit too and then peel those little Pieces as well. Super easy!

Mix the marinade into a frying pan and marinate the fish in the pan on low, low heat while preparing the mango salsa, very slowly the marinade with evaporate off. 
Place frozen mango/strawberry Caribbean fruit and other salsa ingredients into Pampered Chef salsa maker. Used tsp's rather than tbsp's of lemon and lime. Chopped while a little frozen to maintain shape.
Once the salsa is finished, set aside and fry the fish. May have to add butter while frying.

Excellent!! I marinated the fish a few hours ahead of time. Warmed up a cast iron skillet with a little of the oil marinate. Then cooked on stove top until fish was no longer transparent, about 3 mins per side. Served over cooked rice mixed with cranberries, green onions, and pecans. Made the Mango Salsa...Delicious!! Will definitely add this recipe to our rotation for Tilapia.

I don't own a grill so I decided to bake it in a glass pan at 425 degrees Fahrenheit for 15 minutes and it was delicious! I added a little slice of butter on top of each filet before placing it in the over. 10/10 would eat again. I also made the mango salsa which was delicious. Definitely would make great taco and I am trying that next time.

Bearutiful presentation. My guests who are foodies were wowed. They loved it and so did my husband who normally prefers tartar sauce with his fish. I used Sea Bass and served over Saffron rice with asparagus. Every body wanted the recipe. Dicing the Mangos was easy once I got the hang of it. Once I sliced it along the sides of the pit, I made small hash marks down to the skin, then cut it in half to create small dice, then scooped out what was left in the skin. Much easier than removing whole side and then trying to dice into small pieces. It does take a while to do the salsa, make it a day ahead to allow the flavors to meld.

I used canola oil instead of olive oil. I let it marinade for about 3 hours. I left out the jalapenos. I used canned diced mangos drained. I baked it with the marinade covered at 350 for 15 minutes and then uncovered for another 10 minutes. My husband and I loved it. I will definitely make it again!

I have made this recipe hundreds of times and I cannot believe that I’ve never reviewed it. I almost always double or triple the salsa and I have made it with chicken breast as well as other kinds of fish. I do marinate the chicken breast a little longer than 20 minutes. Often mix up the salsa and marinate the chicken in the morning. That way the salsa has a chance for all the flavors to mix together. I think this recipe is delicious. leftovers are pretty good for a day. After that the salsa gets a little mushy I usually serve it with black beans and rice or a different kind of rice dish. This is my kids' favorite meal.

I have made this multiple times, with other fish fillets as well and it is amazing! I have also used the marinade without the salsa and my family has loved it. 
The only thing I do not like is that I feel like the marinade is to much. I prefer to use double fish with the same measurements listed in the recipe. 
I also do not grill, I bake in the oven

I didn't have time to marinate it so I added a little olive oil and garlic to the salsa. I liked it so much that I do that all of the time. I've made this several time now. Friends rave about it. My husband even eats fish that doesn't have to be deep fried now and he'll eat the salsa with a spoon!

Made as written except I used fresh basil instead of dried just because I had it and baked the fish at 375 for about 12-15 minutes because it was storming too badly outside to grill anything! The results were fantastic!! I did double the mango salsa because my family loves it and it was totally gone!! I found some perfectly ripe mangoes at the store (unusual where I live) and they were just bursting with flavor in this salsa. It went so well with the fish! A definite keeper and will be making this often!! Thanks for posting!
Great recipe! Loved the flavor, grilled it on my smoker/pellet grill and served with coconut rice!! Family loved it!!

The flavor of the fish was so good! I didn't cook it on the grill but used a cast iron griddle on the stove. It had a great smoky flavor.... maybe the well-used grill? Served over broccoli "rice" that was bar boiled and topped with the mango salsa. Such a pretty meal served with baked delicata squash with lime butter from this site too!

I am so happy I tried this recipe. I don't cook often and my family was absolutely delighted. The flavors were amazing and it was easy to do. I baked it since I don't have a grill (I did the 15 min covered, 10 min uncovered at 350 degrees option) and we tried it on tortillas. Wonderful fancy fish tacos!
This one goes into the regular rotation, and I may never make tilapia any other way again! I baked the fish in my oven since it's zero degrees outside, but I can't wait to try it on the grill.
Made this for dinner and served over a bed of lentils. Delicious! Added celery to salsa and skipped salt. Will double lime juice next time for a little more citrus complement to the mango.
Better than I expected. I am not a fan of fish and I enjoyed eating this.
This works perfectly with chicken breasts! I marinade and cook a little longer but otherwise, generally follow the same recipe. Delicious.
This mango salsa is amazing on whatever fish you decide to cook. The best flavor of sweet with a little spicy! And so good for you:)

I have made this twice now and we really like it. You may not understand that that is high praise from me. I don't like rice and rarely care for fish. I do use a mango salsa that I already have the recipe for instead of this one, because I think mine is easier.
